text:
Blake Coleman is 34, a two-time Cup winner in his first season in Minnesota, and he's been exactly what the 12-3-4 Wild hoped for: a third-line forward who does the hard parts. He scored 55 seconds into Saturday's game against Tampa Bay, his first goal in seven games, and has five on the season.

His finishing is right where his chances say it should be (five goals on 5.8 expected, the quality of his chances). Nothing here is luck in either direction. Minnesota is slightly better at five on five when he sits than when he plays this year, which is a small-sample quirk worth watching but not worrying about yet.

Last season he was much more than a checker. Evolving-Hockey had him 58th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, driving play at one end (86th percentile) and taking it away at the other (96th). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net often (87th percentile). Our projection sees about 23 goals.
